title: Ameliorative effects of bilirubin on cell culture model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
authors: Vakili, Omid; Borji, Mohammad; Saffari-Chaleshtori, Javad; Shafiee, Sayed Mohammad
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胆红素对非酒精性脂肪肝细胞模型的影响，涉及基因表达和简单对接，但核心是代谢疾病而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is defined as the most prevalent hepatic disorder that affects a significant population worldwide. There are several genes/proteins, involving in the modulation of NAFLD pathogenesis; sirtuin1 (SIRT1), TP53-inducible regulator gene (TIGAR), and autophagy-related gene 5 (Atg5) are considered a chief group of these modulators that principally act by regulating the hepatic lipid metabolism, as well as preventing the lipid accumulation. Surprisingly, bilirubin, especially in its unconjugated form, might be able to alleviate NAFLD progression by decreasing lipid accumulation and regulating the expression levels of the above-stated genes. METHODS AND RESULTS: Herein, the interactions between bilirubin and the corresponding genes' products were first analyzed by docking assessments. Afterwards, HepG2 cells were cultured under the optimum conditions, and then were incubated with high concentrations of glucose to induce NAFLD. After treating normal and fatty liver cells with particular bilirubin concentrations for 24- and 48-hour periods, 3-[4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl]-2,5-diphenyl-tetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay, colorimetric method, and quantitative reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were employed to assess cell viability status, intracellular triglycerides content, and mRNA expression levels of the genes, respectively. Intracellular lipid accumulation of HepG2 cells was significantly decreased after treating with bilirubin. Bilirubin also increased SIRT1 and Atg5 gene expression levels in fatty liver cells. TIGAR gene expression levels were variable upon the conditions and the cell type, suggesting a dual role for TIGAR during the NAFLD pathogenesis. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate the potential of bilirubin in the prevention from or amelioration of NAFLD through influencing SIRT1-related deacetylation and the process of lipophagy, as well as decreasing the intrahepatic lipid content. In vitro model of NAFLD was treated with unconjugated bilirubin under the optimal conditions.Desirably, bilirubin moderated the accumulation of triglycerides within the cells possibly through modulation of the expression of SIRT1, Atg5, and TIGAR genes. In the context, bilirubin was shown to increase the expression levels of SIRT1 and Atg5, while the expression of TIGAR was demonstrated to be either increased or decreased, depending on the treatment conditions. abstract_zh: 背景：非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）被定义为影响全球大量人群的最普遍肝脏疾病。有多种基因/蛋白质参与调节NAFLD的发病机制；其中，sirtuin1（SIRT1）、TP53诱导性调节基因（TIGAR）和自噬相关基因5（Atg5）被认为是这些调节因子中的主要群体，它们主要通过调节肝脏脂质代谢以及防止脂质积累来发挥作用。令人惊讶的是，胆红素，尤其是其非结合形式，可能通过减少脂质积累和调节上述基因的表达水平来缓解NAFLD的进展。方法与结果：在此，首先通过对接评估分析了胆红素与相应基因产物之间的相互作用。随后，在最佳条件下培养HepG2细胞，并与高浓度葡萄糖孵育以诱导NAFLD。在将正常和脂肪肝细胞与特定浓度的胆红素处理24小时和48小时后，采用3-[4,5-二甲基噻唑-2-基]-2,5-二苯基四唑溴化物（MTT）检测、比色法和定量逆转录聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）分别评估细胞活力状态、细胞内甘油三酯含量和基因的mRNA表达水平。经胆红素处理后，HepG2细胞内的脂质积累显著减少。胆红素还增加了脂肪肝细胞中SIRT1和Atg5基因的表达水平。TIGAR基因的表达水平随条件和细胞类型而变化，提示TIGAR在NAFLD发病机制中具有双重作用。结论：我们的研究结果表明，胆红素通过影响SIRT1相关的去乙酰化和脂噬过程，以及降低肝内脂质含量，具有预防或改善NAFLD的潜力。在最佳条件下，用非结合胆红素处理NAFLD的体外模型。理想情况下，胆红素可能通过调节SIRT1、Atg5和TIGAR基因的表达来调节细胞内甘油三酯的积累。在此背景下，胆红素被证明能增加SIRT1和Atg5的表达水平，而TIGAR的表达则根据处理条件被证明是增加或减少。使用BioRender.com创建。
